summary: Stellar Explorer is an interactive astronomy platform inspired by NASA’s SPHEREx mission. It aims to make astronomical data accessible through immersive visualisations and educational tools. Users can explore thousands of celestial objects through an interactive 3D sky, investigate light spectra to understand the composition of stars and molecular clouds, and compare observations from different telescopes. Its features include SPHEREx Sees, Dips & Peaks, and Sky Lab, which offers image comparisons, observation timelines, and a visualisation of cosmic history. By combining real astronomical datasets, interactive exploration, and scientific explanations, Stellar Explorer bridges the gap between complex space research and public understanding of the universe.
details:
Stellar Explorer is an interactive astronomy platform inspired by NASA’s SPHEREx mission. It transforms complex astronomical information into an engaging experience through three main tools. SPHEREx Sees allows users to explore a 3D representation of the night sky and discover celestial objects. Dips & Peaks introduces spectroscopy, helping users understand how scientists identify elements and molecules through light. Sky Lab allows users to compare telescope observations, explore changes over time, and visualise the evolution of the universe.

The project aims to make astronomy more accessible, encourage scientific curiosity, and help users understand how space research works. Its intended impact is to bridge the gap between scientific data and public understanding.

The platform is developed using Base44, with web technologies and interactive visualisation features. It is designed around astronomical datasets and imagery, particularly those associated with SPHEREx. Its creativity lies in combining scientific exploration, interactive learning, and visual storytelling within one platform.

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, user experience, visual appeal, and educational value. We also aimed to distinguish genuine astronomical observations from conceptual simulations, ensuring that the platform remains both engaging and scientifically responsible.
